solution:
We use \(\tan^{-1}(1)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\), \(\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{3}\) and \(\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{6}\).
\(\therefore \tan^{-1}(1)+\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)+\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}+\dfrac{\pi}{3}+\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac{3\pi+4\pi+2\pi}{12}=\dfrac{9\pi}{12}=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\).
Hence the value is \(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\).

We use \(\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{3}\) and \(\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{6}\).
\(\therefore \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)+2\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{3}+2\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac{\pi}{3}+\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\).
Hence the value is \(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\).

\(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{3}=\dfrac{\pi}{3}\). The principal range of \(\sec^{-1}\) is \([0,\pi]\setminus\left\{\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right\}\), so \(\sec^{-1}(-2)=\pi-\sec^{-1}(2)=\pi-\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\).
\(\therefore \tan^{-1}\sqrt{3}-\sec^{-1}(-2)=\dfrac{\pi}{3}-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}=-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\).
Hence the value is \(-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\).

The principal range of \(\csc^{-1}\) is \(\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\setminus\{0\}\), so \(\csc^{-1}(-\sqrt{2})=-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\). Also \(\cot^{-1}(\sqrt{3})=\dfrac{\pi}{6}\).
\(\therefore \csc^{-1}(-\sqrt{2})+\cot^{-1}(\sqrt{3})=-\dfrac{\pi}{4}+\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac{-3\pi+2\pi}{12}=-\dfrac{\pi}{12}\).
Hence the value is \(-\dfrac{\pi}{12}\).

We use \(\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\) and \(\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{3}\).
\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)-3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-3\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\pi=\dfrac{\pi-4\pi}{4}=-\dfrac{3\pi}{4}=\) R.H.S.
Hence proved.

\(\sin^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\). Also \(\cos^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)=\pi-\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)=\pi-\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\).
\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(=-\dfrac{\pi}{6}+\dfrac{5\pi}{6}=\dfrac{4\pi}{6}=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\).
Also R.H.S. \(=\cos^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=\pi-\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=\pi-\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\).
\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(=\) R.H.S. Hence proved.

Let \(A=\sin^{-1}\dfrac{3}{5}\), so \(\sin A=\dfrac{3}{5}\) and \(\cos A=\dfrac{4}{5}\) (\(A\) acute). Let \(B=\cos^{-1}\dfrac{12}{13}\), so \(\cos B=\dfrac{12}{13}\) and \(\sin B=\dfrac{5}{13}\) (\(B\) acute).
\(\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B=\dfrac{3}{5}\cdot\dfrac{12}{13}+\dfrac{4}{5}\cdot\dfrac{5}{13}=\dfrac{36}{65}+\dfrac{20}{65}=\dfrac{56}{65}\).
Since \(A,B\) are acute and \(A+B\) is acute, \(A+B=\sin^{-1}\dfrac{56}{65}\).
\(\therefore \sin^{-1}\dfrac{3}{5}+\cos^{-1}\dfrac{12}{13}=\sin^{-1}\dfrac{56}{65}\). Hence proved.

Let \(A=\cos^{-1}\dfrac{3}{5}\), so \(\cos A=\dfrac{3}{5}\) and \(\sin A=\dfrac{4}{5}\). Let \(B=\cos^{-1}\dfrac{4}{5}\), so \(\cos B=\dfrac{4}{5}\) and \(\sin B=\dfrac{3}{5}\).
\(\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B=\dfrac{3}{5}\cdot\dfrac{4}{5}-\dfrac{4}{5}\cdot\dfrac{3}{5}=\dfrac{12}{25}-\dfrac{12}{25}=0\).
Since \(A,B\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\), \(A+B\in(0,\pi)\), and \(\cos(A+B)=0\Rightarrow A+B=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\).
\(\therefore \cos^{-1}\dfrac{3}{5}+\cos^{-1}\dfrac{4}{5}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\). Hence proved.

Here the product \(\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{3}=\dfrac{1}{6}<1\), so
\(\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2}+\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}}{1-\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{3}}\right)=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\frac{5}{6}}{\frac{5}{6}}\right)=\tan^{-1}(1)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\). Hence proved.

Using \(2\tan^{-1}x=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2x}{1-x^{2}}\) (valid for \(|x|<1\)) with \(x=\dfrac{1}{3}\):
\(2\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2\cdot\frac{1}{3}}{1-\frac{1}{9}}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\frac{2}{3}}{\frac{8}{9}}=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\cdot\dfrac{9}{8}\right)=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{3}{4}\). Hence proved.

Dividing the numerator and denominator by \(\cos\theta\):
\(\dfrac{\cos\theta+\sin\theta}{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}=\dfrac{1+\tan\theta}{1-\tan\theta}=\dfrac{\tan\frac{\pi}{4}+\tan\theta}{1-\tan\frac{\pi}{4}\tan\theta}=\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}+\theta\right)\).
\(\therefore \tan^{-1}\left[\dfrac{\cos\theta+\sin\theta}{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}\right]=\tan^{-1}\left[\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}+\theta\right)\right]\).
For \(\theta\in\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4},\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\), \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}+\theta\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\subset\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\), so \(\tan^{-1}\left[\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}+\theta\right)\right]=\dfrac{\pi}{4}+\theta\). Hence proved.

Using \(1-\cos\theta=2\sin^{2}\dfrac{\theta}{2}\) and \(1+\cos\theta=2\cos^{2}\dfrac{\theta}{2}\):
\(\sqrt{\dfrac{1-\cos\theta}{1+\cos\theta}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{2\sin^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}}{2\cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}}}=\left|\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right|\).
For \(\theta\in(0,\pi)\), \(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\), so \(\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}>0\) and the expression equals \(\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}\).
\(\therefore \tan^{-1}\sqrt{\dfrac{1-\cos\theta}{1+\cos\theta}}=\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)=\dfrac{\theta}{2}\) (as \(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\)). Hence proved.

Let \(\alpha=\sin^{-1}\dfrac{3}{5}\), so \(\sin\alpha=\dfrac{3}{5},\ \cos\alpha=\dfrac{4}{5},\ \tan\alpha=\dfrac{3}{4}\), with \(\alpha\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\).
\(\tan 2\alpha=\dfrac{2\tan\alpha}{1-\tan^{2}\alpha}=\dfrac{2\cdot\frac{3}{4}}{1-\frac{9}{16}}=\dfrac{\frac{3}{2}}{\frac{7}{16}}=\dfrac{3}{2}\cdot\dfrac{16}{7}=\dfrac{24}{7}\).
Since \(\alpha\approx 36.87^{\circ}\), \(2\alpha\approx 73.74^{\circ}\in\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\), so \(2\alpha=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{24}{7}\).
\(\therefore 2\sin^{-1}\dfrac{3}{5}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{24}{7}\). Hence proved.

Put \(\sqrt{x}=\tan\theta\), i.e. \(\theta=\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x}\). For \(x\in[0,1]\), \(\theta\in\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]\) and \(x=\tan^{2}\theta\).
\(\dfrac{1-x}{1+x}=\dfrac{1-\tan^{2}\theta}{1+\tan^{2}\theta}=\cos 2\theta\).
\(\therefore \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1-x}{1+x}\right)=\cos^{-1}(\cos 2\theta)=2\theta\) (since \(2\theta\in\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]\subset[0,\pi]\)).
\(\therefore \dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1-x}{1+x}\right)=\theta=\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x}\). Hence proved.

Let \(\alpha=\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}\), so \(\sin\alpha=\dfrac{1}{3}\) and \(\cos\alpha=\sqrt{1-\dfrac{1}{9}}=\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\). Hence \(\sin^{-1}\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}=\cos^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}\) (complementary angle), so
\(\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}+\sin^{-1}\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}=\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}+\cos^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\).
Multiplying throughout by \(\dfrac{9}{4}\):
\(\dfrac{9}{4}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}+\dfrac{9}{4}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}=\dfrac{9}{4}\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{2}=\dfrac{9\pi}{8}\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{9\pi}{8}-\dfrac{9}{4}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}=\dfrac{9}{4}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\). Hence proved.
[Textbook misprint: the printed left-hand constant \(\dfrac{9\pi}{5}\) should be \(\dfrac{9\pi}{8}\); the identity holds only with \(\dfrac{9\pi}{8}\) (numerically both sides equal \(2.770\)).]

Put \(x=\cos 2\theta\), so \(2\theta=\cos^{-1}x\), i.e. \(\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}x\). For \(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\le x\le 1\), \(\cos^{-1}x\in\left[0,\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right]\), so \(\theta\in\left[0,\dfrac{3\pi}{8}\right]\) and \(\cos\theta\ge 0,\ \sin\theta\ge 0\).
\(\sqrt{1+x}=\sqrt{1+\cos 2\theta}=\sqrt{2\cos^{2}\theta}=\sqrt{2}\cos\theta\), and \(\sqrt{1-x}=\sqrt{2\sin^{2}\theta}=\sqrt{2}\sin\theta\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{\sqrt{1+x}-\sqrt{1-x}}{\sqrt{1+x}+\sqrt{1-x}}=\dfrac{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}{\cos\theta+\sin\theta}=\dfrac{1-\tan\theta}{1+\tan\theta}=\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\theta\right)\).
Since \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\theta\in\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{8},\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]\subset\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\),
\(\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{1+x}-\sqrt{1-x}}{\sqrt{1+x}+\sqrt{1-x}}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}x\). Hence proved.

\(\sin\left(\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{5}+\cos^{-1}x\right)=1\Rightarrow \sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{5}+\cos^{-1}x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\).
\(\therefore \cos^{-1}x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{5}=\cos^{-1}\dfrac{1}{5}\) (using \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\sin^{-1}t=\cos^{-1}t\)).
\(\therefore x=\dfrac{1}{5}\).

[Textbook misprint: the right-hand side should read \(\tan^{-1}(2\csc x)\); as printed with \(\csc x\) the equation gives \(\tan x=2\), a non-standard angle. Solving the intended equation \(2\tan^{-1}(\cos x)=\tan^{-1}(2\csc x)\):]
\(2\tan^{-1}(\cos x)=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2\cos x}{1-\cos^{2}x}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2\cos x}{\sin^{2}x}\).
Equating with \(\tan^{-1}(2\csc x)=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2}{\sin x}\):
\(\dfrac{2\cos x}{\sin^{2}x}=\dfrac{2}{\sin x}\Rightarrow \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin^{2}x}=\dfrac{1}{\sin x}\Rightarrow \cos x=\sin x\Rightarrow \tan x=1\).
\(\therefore x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\).

For \(x>0\), \(\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1-x}{1+x}\right)=\tan^{-1}(1)-\tan^{-1}x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\tan^{-1}x\).
The equation becomes \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\tan^{-1}x=\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}x\Rightarrow \dfrac{\pi}{4}=\dfrac{3}{2}\tan^{-1}x\Rightarrow \tan^{-1}x=\dfrac{\pi}{6}\).
\(\therefore x=\tan\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).

Let \(\sin^{-1}x=\alpha\), so \(x=\sin\alpha\). The equation gives \(\sin^{-1}(1-x)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}+2\alpha\).
Taking sine of both sides: \(1-x=\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}+2\alpha\right)=\cos 2\alpha=1-2\sin^{2}\alpha=1-2x^{2}\).
\(\therefore 1-x=1-2x^{2}\Rightarrow 2x^{2}-x=0\Rightarrow x(2x-1)=0\Rightarrow x=0\ \text{or}\ x=\dfrac{1}{2}\).
Check: \(x=0\) gives \(\sin^{-1}(1)-0=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\) (valid). \(x=\dfrac{1}{2}\) gives \(\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2}-2\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2}=-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\ne\dfrac{\pi}{2}\) (rejected).
\(\therefore x=0\).

\(\tan^{-1}2x+\tan^{-1}3x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\Rightarrow \tan^{-1}3x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\tan^{-1}2x=\cot^{-1}2x=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2x}\) (for \(x>0\)).
\(\therefore 3x=\dfrac{1}{2x}\Rightarrow 6x^{2}=1\Rightarrow x^{2}=\dfrac{1}{6}\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\).
\(\therefore x=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\).
[Note: if the intended right-hand side is \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\) rather than \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\), then \(\dfrac{5x}{1-6x^{2}}=1\Rightarrow 6x^{2}+5x-1=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{1}{6}\).]

\(\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2}-\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{4}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{4}}{1+\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{4}}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\frac{1}{4}}{\frac{9}{8}}=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{8}{9}\right)=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2}{9}\). Hence proved.

Note \(\cot^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}=\tan^{-1}3\) (since \(\cot\theta=\dfrac{1}{3}\Rightarrow \tan\theta=3\)).
\(\therefore \cot^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}-\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}=\tan^{-1}3-\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{3-\frac{1}{3}}{1+3\cdot\frac{1}{3}}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\frac{8}{3}}{2}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{4}{3}\).
Also \(\cot^{-1}\dfrac{3}{4}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{4}{3}\).
\(\therefore \cot^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}-\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}=\cot^{-1}\dfrac{3}{4}\). Hence proved.

Let \(\theta=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2}\), so \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}\).
\(\tan 3\theta=\dfrac{3\tan\theta-\tan^{3}\theta}{1-3\tan^{2}\theta}=\dfrac{3\cdot\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{8}}{1-3\cdot\frac{1}{4}}=\dfrac{\frac{12}{8}-\frac{1}{8}}{\frac{1}{4}}=\dfrac{\frac{11}{8}}{\frac{1}{4}}=\dfrac{11}{2}\).
Since \(\theta\approx 26.57^{\circ}\), \(3\theta\approx 79.7^{\circ}\in\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\), so \(3\theta=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{11}{2}\), i.e. \(3\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{11}{2}\).
\(\therefore \tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{11}{2}\). Hence proved.

We use \(\cos^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\dfrac{\pi}{6}\) and \(\sin^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\dfrac{\pi}{3}\).
\(\therefore \cos^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+2\sin^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\dfrac{\pi}{6}+2\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\dfrac{\pi}{6}+\dfrac{4\pi}{6}=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\). Hence proved.

Let \(\alpha=\cot^{-1}\dfrac{3}{2}\), so \(\tan\alpha=\dfrac{2}{3}\). Then \(\tan 2\alpha=\dfrac{2\cdot\frac{2}{3}}{1-\frac{4}{9}}=\dfrac{\frac{4}{3}}{\frac{5}{9}}=\dfrac{12}{5}\), so \(2\cot^{-1}\dfrac{3}{2}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{12}{5}\).
For \(\sec^{-1}\dfrac{13}{12}\): \(\sec\beta=\dfrac{13}{12}\Rightarrow \cos\beta=\dfrac{12}{13},\ \tan\beta=\dfrac{5}{12}\), so \(\sec^{-1}\dfrac{13}{12}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{5}{12}\).
\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{12}{5}+\tan^{-1}\dfrac{5}{12}\). Since \(\dfrac{12}{5}\) and \(\dfrac{5}{12}\) are reciprocals (both positive), \(\tan^{-1}\dfrac{12}{5}+\tan^{-1}\dfrac{5}{12}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\).
\(\therefore 2\cot^{-1}\dfrac{3}{2}+\sec^{-1}\dfrac{13}{12}=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\). Hence proved.

[Textbook misprint: the condition should be \(x>0\); for \(x<0\) the identity fails (L.H.S. is obtuse while R.H.S. is negative) and the correct form is Q.35(ii).]
Proof for \(x>0\): Let \(\cos^{-1}x=\theta\). For \(x>0\), \(\theta\in\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\), with \(\cos\theta=x\) and \(\sin\theta=\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\ge 0\).
\(\therefore \tan\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{x}\), and since \(\theta\in\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\), \(\theta=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{x}\).
\(\therefore \cos^{-1}x=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{x}\). Hence proved.

Let \(\cos^{-1}x=\theta\). For \(x<0\), \(\theta\in\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},\pi\right]\), with \(\cos\theta=x<0\) and \(\sin\theta=\sqrt{1-x^{2}}>0\), so \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{x}<0\).
Let \(\phi=\theta-\pi\in\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right]\). Then \(\tan\phi=\tan(\theta-\pi)=\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{x}\), and since \(\phi\in\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\), \(\phi=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{x}\).
\(\therefore \theta=\pi+\phi=\pi+\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{x}\), i.e. \(\cos^{-1}x=\pi+\tan^{-1}\dfrac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{x}\) for \(x<0\). Hence proved.

Put \(x=\tan\theta\), so \(\theta=\tan^{-1}x\). For \(|x|<1\), \(\theta\in\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4},\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\), hence \(2\theta\in\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\).
(1) \(\dfrac{2x}{1-x^{2}}=\dfrac{2\tan\theta}{1-\tan^{2}\theta}=\tan 2\theta\Rightarrow \tan^{-1}\dfrac{2x}{1-x^{2}}=2\theta=2\tan^{-1}x\).
(2) \(\dfrac{2x}{1+x^{2}}=\dfrac{2\tan\theta}{1+\tan^{2}\theta}=\sin 2\theta\Rightarrow \sin^{-1}\dfrac{2x}{1+x^{2}}=2\theta=2\tan^{-1}x\).
(3) \(\dfrac{1-x^{2}}{1+x^{2}}=\dfrac{1-\tan^{2}\theta}{1+\tan^{2}\theta}=\cos 2\theta\Rightarrow \cos^{-1}\dfrac{1-x^{2}}{1+x^{2}}=2\theta=2\tan^{-1}x\) (for \(0\le x<1\), where \(2\theta\in[0,\pi)\)).
\(\therefore 2\tan^{-1}x=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2x}{1-x^{2}}=\sin^{-1}\dfrac{2x}{1+x^{2}}=\cos^{-1}\dfrac{1-x^{2}}{1+x^{2}}\). Hence proved.

For positive \(x,y,z\), \(ab>0>-1\) in each pair, so \(\tan^{-1}a-\tan^{-1}b=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{a-b}{1+ab}\) applies:
\(\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x-y}{1+xy}=\tan^{-1}x-\tan^{-1}y\),
\(\tan^{-1}\dfrac{y-z}{1+yz}=\tan^{-1}y-\tan^{-1}z\),
\(\tan^{-1}\dfrac{z-x}{1+zx}=\tan^{-1}z-\tan^{-1}x\).
Adding: \((\tan^{-1}x-\tan^{-1}y)+(\tan^{-1}y-\tan^{-1}z)+(\tan^{-1}z-\tan^{-1}x)=0\).
\(\therefore \tan^{-1}\dfrac{x-y}{1+xy}+\tan^{-1}\dfrac{y-z}{1+yz}+\tan^{-1}\dfrac{z-x}{1+zx}=0\). Hence proved.

Given \(\tan^{-1}x+\tan^{-1}y+\tan^{-1}z=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\), so \(\tan^{-1}x+\tan^{-1}y=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\tan^{-1}z\).
Taking tangent of both sides: \(\tan(\tan^{-1}x+\tan^{-1}y)=\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\tan^{-1}z\right)=\cot(\tan^{-1}z)=\dfrac{1}{z}\).
\(\therefore \dfrac{x+y}{1-xy}=\dfrac{1}{z}\Rightarrow z(x+y)=1-xy\Rightarrow zx+zy+xy=1\).
\(\therefore xy+yz+zx=1\). Hence proved.

Let \(\cos^{-1}x=A,\ \cos^{-1}y=B,\ \cos^{-1}z=C\), so \(\cos A=x,\ \cos B=y,\ \cos C=z\) and \(A+B+C=\pi\).
Then \(A+B=\pi-C\), so \(\cos(A+B)=\cos(\pi-C)=-\cos C=-z\).
Also \(\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B=xy-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\sqrt{1-y^{2}}\).
\(\therefore xy-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\sqrt{1-y^{2}}=-z\Rightarrow \sqrt{1-x^{2}}\sqrt{1-y^{2}}=xy+z\).
Squaring both sides: \((1-x^{2})(1-y^{2})=(xy+z)^{2}\)
\(\Rightarrow 1-x^{2}-y^{2}+x^{2}y^{2}=x^{2}y^{2}+2xyz+z^{2}\)
\(\Rightarrow 1-x^{2}-y^{2}=2xyz+z^{2}\).
\(\therefore x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}+2xyz=1\). Hence proved.
